public.prompt: A dashboard requests details for product IDs in display order. Network responses finish in a different order, but each result must still be paired with the ID at the same input index. Which aggregation provides that ordering contract when every request fulfills?

options.label: Push each fulfillment into a shared array, then pair that array with product IDs by position.
Await `Promise.all(requests)`, then pair its result array with product IDs by input position.
Await `Promise.race(requests)` repeatedly, then pair each winner with product IDs by position.

answerProof.summary: Promise.all fulfills with values in iterable order, so completion timing does not change the index relationship between requests and results.
decisiveConstraints: Every input request is assumed to fulfill.
The input array order already matches the display order.
The mapping must not depend on network completion order.

claims.statement: Promise.all returns fulfillment values in the order of the input iterable regardless of the order in which the input promises settle.

optionRationales.explanation: Independent fulfillment handlers append in completion order, so array positions can drift from product IDs.
optionRationales.plausibility: Collecting results as requests finish is simple and avoids waiting before storing each value.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: A slower earlier request must retain its earlier display index.

optionRationales.explanation: Promise.all preserves iterable positions in its fulfilled result array even when requests finish out of order.
Promise.race exposes settlement winners and does not remove settled inputs, so repeating it does not produce an indexed batch.
optionRationales.plausibility: Racing requests appears to provide direct access to their actual completion order.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: The result must retain a stable one-to-one index mapping for the complete input batch.
